mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 declines by over 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of sustained unemployment rate increases above 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of episodes where INDPRO declines by >0.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% in the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls by >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of months where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by >0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and a rise in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% month-over-month signals robust demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise by >2% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during months when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise by >2% MoM (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as earnings growth accelerates.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% and remains there for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher when the unemployment rate stays below 5% for six consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above 0.5% for five consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which lifts corporate revenues and profits and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises by >0.5% for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods when RSAFS rises by >0.5% for five consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).
